text: Dean Withers was accused of R.A.P.E. There are claims involving a girl, claims involving multiple underage men, Dean crashed out on livestream, and now both the left and the right are accusing each other of hypocrisy. So what actually happened there? Let's start from the beginning. As best as I can trace it, this started around August 10, when a TikTok account called Emily began making extremely serious allegations against Dean. The account claimed Dean had S.A.I.D. and R.A.P.E'd her, posting things like, I was just a kid, I didn't deserve that, and saying that people were defending Dean instead of believing her. And importantly, there was supposedly evidence. The account posted screenshots of alleged messages between Emily and Dean, including one where Dean supposedly says that he was drunk, barely remembered a night, and tells her to leave it alone. So obviously, if those messages were real, that would look pretty bad. The allegations started spreading, and by August 15, they had made their way heavily onto political Twitter. A Groyper-associated account posted a clip of Dean reacting to the accusations, saying, the Groyper curse is pretty scary, man, and it went viral. But then there was a pretty major problem with the original accusation. A girl came forward, saying the pictures Emily was using were actually hers. She is reportedly a 13-year-old girl from Australia. She showed what she said were the original pictures and said she had absolutely nothing to do with the accusations against Dean. Now, technically, that alone doesn't prove that there isn't some other anonymous girl behind the account. Someone could theoretically hide their real identity because they don't want people knowing who they are. But if you're pretending that somebody else's pictures are you while making an R.A.P.E. accusation, there is already a gigantic credibility problem. And then we get to the alleged DMs. Dean responded by pointing out several apparent inconsistencies in the screenshots. He pointed out that screenshots allegedly showing messages from his account don't show the verification badge on his profile. He also claimed that two screenshots supposedly showing the same conversation don't seem to line up properly. A date and time appears in one screenshot but disappears in another. Dean says this proves that the messages are fake. Personally, I wouldn't go quite that far without the original files or some proper forensic analysis. I don't think a weird screenshot automatically proves fabrication. But combine questionable screenshots with the serious questions surrounding the identity of Emily and at the very least, the original accusation becomes extremely difficult to take as credible evidence. Then another accusation started spreading that multiple underage male victims had also accused Dean of S.A. But this part is actually much simpler. So far, I haven't found identifiable accusers or independent evidence substantiating those claims. Not even anything comparable to the material posted by Emily. So until actual evidence emerges, there's not much more we can say about that. And while all of this was spreading, Dean was obviously not taking it particularly well. People kept flooding his live streams with accusations and confronting him about the supposed evidence. And on August 16, after arguing with callers about the allegations, Dean eventually became extremely emotional and broke down crying on stream. And naturally, those clips went viral too. Dean then released a more formal response where he denied the accusations. But he also made another claim. He said, a Trump supporter stole the identity of an innocent 13-year-old girl to falsely accuse him of R.A.P.E. And he later posted, MAGA, you owe me an apology. And keep that in mind because we're going to come back to it. And once you look at the political reaction, things get pretty interesting. Because there's hypocrisy, there is trolling, and there are criticisms coming from both sides. We talk about political reactions in the next video.
